subproblem.title: Egoroff's theorem for Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ with a closed good set and uniform convergence on compacta
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, let η_k : ℝⁿ → ℝ (k ∈ ℕ) and g : ℝⁿ → ℝ be Borel measurable, let S ⊆ ℝⁿ be a Borel set, and suppose η_k(x) → g(x) as k → ∞ for every x ∈ S. Then for every ε ∈ (0, ∞] there is a closed set A ⊆ S with Lⁿ(S ∖ A) < ε such that η_k → g uniformly on every compact set Q ⊆ A.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (η : ℕ → Rn n → ℝ) (g : Rn n → ℝ) (S : Set (Rn n)), (∀ k, Measurable (η k)) → Measurable g → MeasurableSet S → (∀ x ∈ S, Tendsto (fun k => η k x) atTop (𝓝 (g x))) → ∀ ε : ℝ≥0∞, 0 < ε → ∃ A ⊆ S, IsClosed A ∧ volume (S \ A) < ε ∧ ∀ Q : Set (Rn n), IsCompact Q → Q ⊆ A → TendstoUniformlyOn η g atTop Q
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Simon's proof of Ch. 2, Theorem 1.5, chapter-02.txt lines 260–265: “by Egoroff's Theorem (applied to the finite measure sets C ∩ B_j(0), j = 1, 2, …) there is an Lⁿ-measurable set A₀ ⊆ C such that Lⁿ(C ∖ A₀) < ε/4 and η_k converges uniformly to zero on each bounded subset of A₀. Since we can take a closed set A ⊆ A₀ with Lⁿ(A₀ ∖ A) < ε/4 …”. This is Steps 6–7 of the parent proof, with the closed set C replaced by an arbitrary Borel set S and the limit 0 by an arbitrary Borel function g. The closed inner regularity used is Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 1.15(2) (chapter-01.txt lines 274–285). Notation: |x| is the Euclidean norm, B_r(0) the open ball (B_0(0) := ∅), Lⁿ = volume.

Statement. Let η_k : ℝⁿ → ℝ (k ∈ ℕ) and g : ℝⁿ → ℝ be Borel, S ⊆ ℝⁿ Borel with η_k(x) → g(x) for every x ∈ S, and ε ∈ (0, ∞]. Then there is a closed A ⊆ S with Lⁿ(S ∖ A) < ε such that η_k → g uniformly on every compact Q ⊆ A.

Proof.

1. Choose positive reals δ_j (j = 1, 2, …) with Σ_j δ_j < ε/2. For instance δ_j := 2^{−j−2} min{ε, 1} works: its sum is min{ε, 1}/4 < ε/2, also when ε = ∞.

2. Egoroff on the bounded pieces. Fix j ≥ 1. The set S ∩ B_j(0) is Borel with Lⁿ(S ∩ B_j(0)) ≤ Lⁿ(B_j(0)) < ∞. The functions η_k and g are Borel and real-valued, hence strongly measurable, and η_k(x) → g(x) at every point of S ∩ B_j(0). Egoroff's theorem on a set of finite measure (Lean: MeasureTheory.tendstoUniformlyOn_of_ae_tendsto, module Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.Egorov) gives a Borel set t_j ⊆ S ∩ B_j(0) with Lⁿ(t_j) ≤ δ_j such that η_k → g uniformly on G_j := (S ∩ B_j(0)) ∖ t_j. Each G_j is Borel.

3. The set A₀. Put P_j := G_j ∖ B_{j−1}(0) and A₀ := ⋃_j P_j ⊆ S. If x ∈ S ∖ A₀, let j := ⌊|x|⌋ + 1. Then j − 1 ≤ |x| < j, so x ∈ (S ∩ B_j(0)) ∖ B_{j−1}(0), and since x ∉ P_j we must have x ∈ t_j. Hence S ∖ A₀ ⊆ ⋃_j t_j and Lⁿ(S ∖ A₀) ≤ Σ_j δ_j.

4. Closed pieces. Each P_j is Borel with Lⁿ(P_j) ≤ Lⁿ(B_j(0)) < ∞. By closed inner regularity (Simon 1.15(2); Lean: MeasurableSet.exists_isClosed_sdiff_lt) there is a closed F_j ⊆ P_j with Lⁿ(P_j ∖ F_j) < δ_j. Put A := ⋃_j F_j. Then A ⊆ A₀ ⊆ S. If x ∈ A₀ ∖ A, then x ∈ P_j ∖ F_j for some j; so A₀ ∖ A ⊆ ⋃_j (P_j ∖ F_j) and Lⁿ(A₀ ∖ A) ≤ Σ_j δ_j.

5. A is closed. We have F_j ⊆ P_j ⊆ {x : j − 1 ≤ |x| < j}. If z ∈ ℝⁿ and y ∈ F_j ∩ B_1(z), then j − 1 ≤ |y| < |z| + 1, so B_1(z) meets F_j only for the finitely many j < |z| + 2. Thus (F_j) is a locally finite family of closed sets, and its union A is closed (Lean: LocallyFinite.isClosed_iUnion).

6. Measure estimate. S ∖ A ⊆ (S ∖ A₀) ∪ (A₀ ∖ A) ⊆ ⋃_j t_j ∪ ⋃_j (P_j ∖ F_j). Hence Lⁿ(S ∖ A) ≤ Σ_j δ_j + Σ_j δ_j < ε/2 + ε/2 = ε. This holds in [0, ∞] because Σ_j δ_j is finite.

7. Uniform convergence on compact subsets of A. Let Q ⊆ A be compact. Q is bounded, so Q ⊆ B_R(0) for some real R; choose an integer J ≥ max{R, 1}. If x ∈ Q, then x ∈ F_j for some j with j − 1 ≤ |x| < R ≤ J, so j ≤ J and x ∈ F_j ⊆ P_j ⊆ G_j. Hence Q ⊆ G_1 ∪ … ∪ G_J.
Given e > 0, for each of the finitely many j ≤ J, uniform convergence on G_j gives k_j with |η_k(x) − g(x)| < e for all k ≥ k_j and x ∈ G_j. Then |η_k(x) − g(x)| < e for all k ≥ max{k_1, …, k_J} and all x ∈ Q (Lean: Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff with Filter.eventually_all_finset). So η_k → g uniformly on Q. ∎
proof_key_steps: Choose positive δ_j with Σ δ_j < ε/2.
Egoroff on the finite-measure pieces S ∩ B_j(0): uniform convergence on G_j = (S ∩ B_j(0)) ∖ t_j with Lⁿ(t_j) ≤ δ_j.
A₀ = ⋃_j (G_j ∖ B_{j−1}(0)) satisfies S ∖ A₀ ⊆ ⋃ t_j.
Closed F_j ⊆ G_j ∖ B_{j−1}(0) with defect < δ_j; A = ⋃ F_j is closed by local finiteness, and Lⁿ(S ∖ A) < ε.
A compact Q ⊆ A lies in G_1 ∪ … ∪ G_J, where convergence is uniform; a finite intersection of eventualities gives uniform convergence on Q.

audit.reason: The proposition exactly matches the stated measurability and pointwise-convergence assumptions. Finite-measure Egorov and closed inner regularity produce the annular closed pieces with the claimed error bounds. Local finiteness proves closedness; every compact subset meets finitely many relevant pieces, giving uniform convergence. The finite error budget also handles infinite epsilon. No undeclared child dependency or name conflict occurs.

subproblem.title: Lusin's theorem for Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ: closed subsets of Borel sets, finite-dimensional targets
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, let F be a finite-dimensional real normed space with its Borel σ-algebra, let u : ℝⁿ → F be Borel measurable (ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)), let S ⊆ ℝⁿ be a Borel set and let ε ∈ (0, ∞]. Then there is a closed set C ⊆ S with Lⁿ(S ∖ C) < ε such that the restriction u|C is continuous.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (F : Type) [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] [FiniteDimensional ℝ F] [MeasurableSpace F] [BorelSpace F] (u : Rn n → F) (S : Set (Rn n)), Measurable u → MeasurableSet S → ∀ ε : ℝ≥0∞, 0 < ε → ∃ C ⊆ S, IsClosed C ∧ volume (S \ C) < ε ∧ ContinuousOn u C
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. This is the Lusin step of Simon's proof of Ch. 2, Theorem 1.5 (chapter-02.txt lines 248–251: “By Lusin's theorem (which applies to sets of infinite measure for Lⁿ) there is a closed set C ⊆ B such that ∇f|C is continuous and Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ C) < ε/2”), i.e. Step 4 of the parent proof. Here the differentiability set B is replaced by an arbitrary Borel set S, and ∇f by an arbitrary Borel map u into a finite-dimensional space. The ingredients are Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 1.15(2) (closed inner regularity, chapter-01.txt lines 274–285) and Ch. 1, Theorem 1.17 (Lusin's theorem for real-valued functions on sets of finite measure, chapter-01.txt lines 346–380). Notation: |x| is the Euclidean norm, B_r(0) the open ball of radius r about 0 (B_0(0) := ∅), Lⁿ = volume.

Statement. Let F be a finite-dimensional real normed space with its Borel σ-algebra, u : ℝⁿ → F Borel, S ⊆ ℝⁿ Borel and ε ∈ (0, ∞]. Then there is a closed C ⊆ S with Lⁿ(S ∖ C) < ε and u|C continuous.

Proof.

1. Closed inner regularity. For every Borel T ⊆ ℝⁿ with Lⁿ(T) < ∞ and every δ ∈ (0, ∞] there is a closed F' ⊆ T with Lⁿ(T ∖ F') < δ. This is Simon 1.15(2) for the Radon measure Lⁿ. In Lean, Lebesgue measure on Rn n is weakly regular and the statement is MeasurableSet.exists_isClosed_sdiff_lt.

2. Real-valued Lusin on a set of finite measure. For every Borel T with Lⁿ(T) < ∞, every Borel v : ℝⁿ → ℝ and every δ ∈ (0, ∞] there is a closed C' ⊆ T with Lⁿ(T ∖ C') < δ and v|C' continuous. This is Simon 1.17. In Lean it is Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.exists_isClosed_continuousOn_of_measurable (module Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.Lusin) applied with ν := volume; its regularity hypothesis hreg is exactly Step 1.

3. F-valued Lusin on a set of finite measure. Let T be Borel with Lⁿ(T) < ∞ and δ ∈ (0, ∞]. Let d := dim F, fix a basis b_1, …, b_d of F, and let e : F → ℝ^d be the coordinate isomorphism (Lean: (Module.finBasis ℝ F).equivFunL). Both e and e⁻¹ are linear maps between finite-dimensional spaces, hence continuous. The coordinate functions u_l := (e ∘ u)_l (l = 1, …, d) are Borel, being compositions of the Borel map u with continuous maps.
Choose positive reals δ_0, δ_1, …, δ_d with δ_0 + δ_1 + … + δ_d < δ. By Step 1 there is a closed C^0 ⊆ T with Lⁿ(T ∖ C^0) < δ_0. By Step 2, for each l = 1, …, d there is a closed C^l ⊆ T with Lⁿ(T ∖ C^l) < δ_l and u_l|C^l continuous. Put C_T := C^0 ∩ C^1 ∩ … ∩ C^d.
Then C_T is closed, and C_T ⊆ C^0 ⊆ T; the set C^0 guarantees this inclusion also when d = 0. Moreover T ∖ C_T = ⋃_{l=0}^{d} (T ∖ C^l), so Lⁿ(T ∖ C_T) ≤ Σ_l Lⁿ(T ∖ C^l) < δ. Every u_l is continuous on C_T ⊆ C^l, so e ∘ u is continuous on C_T, because a map into ℝ^d is continuous on a set iff all its coordinates are. Therefore u = e⁻¹ ∘ (e ∘ u) is continuous on C_T.

4. Exhaustion by annuli. For j = 1, 2, … let T_j := S ∩ {x : j − 1 ≤ |x| < j} = S ∩ (B_j(0) ∖ B_{j−1}(0)). Each T_j is Borel with Lⁿ(T_j) ≤ Lⁿ(B_j(0)) < ∞, and S is the disjoint union of the T_j: a point x ∈ S lies in T_j for j = ⌊|x|⌋ + 1.
Choose positive reals ε_j with Σ_{j≥1} ε_j < ε. For instance ε_j := 2^{−j−1} min{ε, 1} works: its sum is min{ε, 1}/2 < ε, also when ε = ∞. By Step 3 there are closed sets C_j ⊆ T_j with Lⁿ(T_j ∖ C_j) < ε_j and u|C_j continuous. Put C := ⋃_{j≥1} C_j. Clearly C ⊆ S.

5. C is closed and u|C is continuous. The family (C_j) is locally finite: if z ∈ ℝⁿ and y ∈ C_j ∩ B_1(z), then j − 1 ≤ |y| < |z| + 1, so the ball B_1(z) meets C_j only for the finitely many j < |z| + 2. A union of a locally finite family of closed sets is closed (Lean: LocallyFinite.isClosed_iUnion), so C is closed. Moreover u is continuous on C by the pasting lemma for locally finite closed families (Lean: LocallyFinite.continuousOn_iUnion): each point of C has a neighbourhood meeting only finitely many C_j, and a map continuous on each of finitely many closed sets is continuous on their union.

6. Measure estimate. If x ∈ S ∖ C, let j be such that x ∈ T_j. Since x ∉ C ⊇ C_j, we have x ∈ T_j ∖ C_j. Hence S ∖ C ⊆ ⋃_j (T_j ∖ C_j), and by countable subadditivity Lⁿ(S ∖ C) ≤ Σ_j Lⁿ(T_j ∖ C_j) ≤ Σ_j ε_j < ε. ∎
proof_key_steps: Closed inner regularity of Lⁿ on finite-measure Borel sets (Simon 1.15(2); MeasurableSet.exists_isClosed_sdiff_lt).
Real-valued finite-measure Lusin (Simon 1.17; SimonGMT exists_isClosed_continuousOn_of_measurable with ν := volume).
F-valued finite-measure case: intersect the closed sets for the basis coordinates of u, plus one inner-regularity set; the errors sum to less than δ.
Exhaust S by the bounded pieces T_j = S ∩ {j−1 ≤ |x| < j} and choose closed C_j ⊆ T_j with errors ε_j, where Σ ε_j < ε.
C = ⋃ C_j is a locally finite union, hence closed, and u|C is continuous by pasting; Lⁿ(S ∖ C) ≤ Σ ε_j < ε.

The proof correctly reduces finite-dimensional targets to scalar coordinates, includes an additional closed subset for dimension zero, and establishes closedness and continuity through locally finite annular pasting. Summable errors give the strict measure bound, including infinite epsilon. The obligation is non-circular and its bare name is unreserved.

subproblem.title: Whitney's remainder hypothesis 1.6(‡) on a large closed subset of the differentiability set
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, K ≥ 0, f : ℝⁿ → ℝ K-Lipschitz, L : ℝⁿ → L(ℝⁿ, ℝ) Borel measurable, S ⊆ ℝⁿ a Borel set, and suppose f is Fréchet differentiable at every x ∈ S with derivative L(x). Then for every ε ∈ (0, ∞] there is a closed set A ⊆ S with Lⁿ(S ∖ A) < ε such that for every compact Q ⊆ A and every ε' > 0 there is δ > 0 with |f(y) − f(x) − L(x)(y − x)| ≤ ε'|y − x| for all x ∈ Q and all y ∈ A with |x − y| < δ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (f : Rn n → ℝ) (K : ℝ≥0) (L : Rn n → (Rn n →L[ℝ] ℝ)) (S : Set (Rn n)), LipschitzWith K f → Measurable L → MeasurableSet S → (∀ x ∈ S, HasFDerivAt f (L x) x) → ∀ ε : ℝ≥0∞, 0 < ε → ∃ A ⊆ S, IsClosed A ∧ volume (S \ A) < ε ∧ ∀ Q : Set (Rn n), IsCompact Q → Q ⊆ A → ∀ ε' : ℝ, 0 < ε' → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ x ∈ Q, ∀ y ∈ A, dist x y < δ → ‖f y - f x - L x (y - x)‖ ≤ ε' * ‖y - x‖
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Simon's proof of Ch. 2, Theorem 1.5, chapter-02.txt lines 251–265. The ingredients are: R(x, y) as in 1.6(‡) (lines 179–181); η_k(x) = sup{|R(x, y)| : y ∈ C ∩ B_{1/k}(x) ∖ {x}} (line 258); “η_k ↓ 0 pointwise in C” (line 260); Egoroff and the closed set A (lines 260–265); “and 1.6(‡) holds” (line 265). This is Steps 5–7 of the parent proof together with the verification of 1.6(‡) in its Step 8. The closed set C is replaced by an arbitrary Borel set S on which f is differentiable, and Df by an arbitrary Borel map L with L(x) = Df(x) on S. The continuity of Df|C, used in the parent's measurability remark, is not needed: continuity of f suffices. Notation: |·| is the Euclidean norm, ‖L(x)‖ the operator norm, Lⁿ = volume, and for y ≠ x, R(x, y) := (f(y) − f(x) − L(x)(y − x))/|y − x|.

Statement. Let f : ℝⁿ → ℝ be K-Lipschitz, L : ℝⁿ → L(ℝⁿ, ℝ) Borel, S ⊆ ℝⁿ Borel, f differentiable at every x ∈ S with derivative L(x), and ε ∈ (0, ∞]. Then there is a closed A ⊆ S with Lⁿ(S ∖ A) < ε such that for every compact Q ⊆ A and every ε' > 0 there is δ > 0 with |f(y) − f(x) − L(x)(y − x)| ≤ ε'|y − x| for all x ∈ Q and y ∈ A with |x − y| < δ.

Proof.

1. The functions η_k. For k ≥ 1 and x, y ∈ ℝⁿ let φ_k(x, y) := |R(x, y)| if 0 < |y − x| < 1/k, and φ_k(x, y) := 0 otherwise. For every x ∈ ℝⁿ let η_k(x) := sup_{y ∈ S} φ_k(x, y) (η_k :≡ 0 if S = ∅). For x ∈ S this is Simon's η_k(x) = sup{|R(x, y)| : y ∈ S ∩ B_{1/k}(x) ∖ {x}} with the convention sup ∅ = 0. We use the same formula at x ∉ S, where the values play no role.
If 0 < |y − x| < 1/k, then |f(y) − f(x)| ≤ K|y − x| and |L(x)(y − x)| ≤ ‖L(x)‖ |y − x|, so |R(x, y)| ≤ K + ‖L(x)‖. Hence 0 ≤ φ_k(x, y) ≤ K + ‖L(x)‖ for all x, y. So η_k(x) is a real number with 0 ≤ η_k(x) ≤ K + ‖L(x)‖, and φ_k(x, y) ≤ η_k(x) for every y ∈ S.

2. η_k → 0 pointwise on S (Simon lines 253, 260). Let x ∈ S and e > 0. Since f is differentiable at x with derivative L(x), there is ρ > 0 such that |f(y) − f(x) − L(x)(y − x)| ≤ (e/2)|y − x| whenever |y − x| < ρ. Let k > 1/ρ. If y ∈ S and 0 < |y − x| < 1/k, then |y − x| < ρ and so φ_k(x, y) = |R(x, y)| ≤ e/2. For all other y ∈ S, φ_k(x, y) = 0. Hence 0 ≤ η_k(x) ≤ e/2 < e for all k > 1/ρ, i.e. η_k(x) → 0.

3. Each η_k is Borel (parent Step 5). Since ℝⁿ is a separable metric space, S has a countable subset D with S ⊆ closure(D) (Lean: TopologicalSpace.IsSeparable.exists_countable_dense_subset).
Fix k and x. We claim η_k(x) = M := sup_{y ∈ D} φ_k(x, y). If S = ∅, then D = ∅ and both sides are 0. Otherwise D ≠ ∅ because S ⊆ closure(D), so M ≥ 0; and M ≤ η_k(x) because D ⊆ S.
For the reverse inequality let y ∈ S. If y lies outside the open shell U := {z : 0 < |z − x| < 1/k}, then φ_k(x, y) = 0 ≤ M. If y ∈ U, the function z ↦ |R(x, z)| = |f(z) − f(x) − L(x)(z − x)|/|z − x| is continuous at z = y, because f is continuous and |y − x| > 0. Since y ∈ closure(D) and U is a neighbourhood of y, there are points z ∈ D ∩ U arbitrarily close to y, and for each of them |R(x, z)| = φ_k(x, z) ≤ M. Letting z → y through D ∩ U gives φ_k(x, y) = |R(x, y)| ≤ M (Lean: le_of_tendsto along 𝓝[D] y, which is non-trivial by mem_closure_iff_nhdsWithin_neBot). Taking the supremum over y ∈ S gives η_k(x) ≤ M, which proves the claim.
Next, for fixed y the function x ↦ φ_k(x, y) is Borel. The set {x : 0 < |y − x| < 1/k} is open, and on it x ↦ |f(y) − f(x) − L(x)(y − x)|/|y − x| is Borel: f is continuous, L is Borel, the evaluation map (T, v) ↦ T v is continuous on L(ℝⁿ, ℝ) × ℝⁿ (so x ↦ L(x)(y − x) is Borel), and x ↦ |y − x| is continuous. Therefore η_k = sup_{y ∈ D} φ_k(·, y) is the pointwise supremum of countably many Borel functions and is finite everywhere, hence Borel (Lean: Measurable.iSup over the countable index type D).

4. Egoroff and the closed set (Simon lines 260–265). Apply the sibling theorem egorov_sigma_finite (Lean: Submission.egorov_closed_subset_uniformOn_compact_volume) to the Borel functions η_k, the Borel limit g :≡ 0, the Borel set S and ε. Its convergence hypothesis, η_k(x) → 0 for x ∈ S, holds by Step 2. It yields a closed A ⊆ S with Lⁿ(S ∖ A) < ε such that η_k → 0 uniformly on every compact Q ⊆ A.

5. The estimate 1.6(‡) on A (Simon line 265). Let Q ⊆ A be compact and ε' > 0. By uniform convergence on Q there is k₀ ≥ 1 with η_{k₀}(x) < ε' for all x ∈ Q. Put δ := 1/k₀ > 0, and let x ∈ Q and y ∈ A with |x − y| < δ. If y = x, both sides of the desired inequality vanish. Otherwise 0 < |y − x| < 1/k₀ and y ∈ A ⊆ S, so by Step 1 |R(x, y)| = φ_{k₀}(x, y) ≤ η_{k₀}(x) < ε'. That is, |f(y) − f(x) − L(x)(y − x)| ≤ ε'|y − x|. ∎
proof_key_steps: Define φ_k(x,y) = |R(x,y)| on the shell 0 < |y−x| < 1/k (0 elsewhere) and η_k(x) = sup_{y∈S} φ_k(x,y); the Lipschitz bound gives 0 ≤ η_k(x) ≤ K + ‖L(x)‖.
Differentiability at x ∈ S with derivative L(x) gives η_k(x) → 0.
Borel measurability: η_k is the supremum over a countable D ⊆ S with S ⊆ closure(D), by continuity of f off the diagonal; each x ↦ φ_k(x,y) is Borel because L is Borel.
Apply the sibling σ-finite Egoroff theorem with limit 0: closed A ⊆ S, Lⁿ(S ∖ A) < ε, uniform convergence on compact subsets of A.
η_{k₀} < ε' on Q gives |f(y) − f(x) − L(x)(y − x)| ≤ ε'|y − x| for y ∈ A, |x − y| < 1/k₀.

audit.reason: The Lean type faithfully states the derivative and compact-uniform remainder hypotheses and conclusion. The Lipschitz estimate bounds each supremum everywhere. Reduction to a countable dense subset is justified by continuity in the second variable on the open shell; Borel measurability of L suffices for measurability in the first variable. The declared Egorov dependency then yields exactly the required remainder estimate. Empty sets and coincident points are covered, and the bare name is unreserved.

subproblem.title: C¹ approximation of real-valued Lipschitz functions (Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.5)
subproblem.statement: For all n ∈ ℕ, K ≥ 0, every K-Lipschitz function f : ℝⁿ → ℝ (ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) and every ε ∈ (0, ∞], there is a function g : ℝⁿ → ℝ of class C¹ such that Lⁿ({x : f(x) ≠ g(x) or Df(x) ≠ Dg(x)}) < ε, where D is Mathlib's Fréchet derivative fderiv (0 at points of non-differentiability).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (f : Rn n → ℝ) (K : ℝ≥0), LipschitzWith K f → ∀ ε : ℝ≥0∞, 0 < ε → ∃ g : Rn n → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 g ∧ volume {x | f x ≠ g x ∨ fderiv ℝ f x ≠ fderiv ℝ g x} < ε
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Simon, Ch. 2, Theorem 1.5 (C¹ Approximation Theorem): statement chapter-02.txt lines 165–168, printed proof lines 246–266. This is Steps 3, 4 and 8 of the parent proof for scalar f. Steps 5–7 are supplied by the sibling uniform_remainder, and the σ-finite Lusin step by the sibling lusin_sigma_finite. Notation: Lⁿ = volume, and Dh(x) = fderiv ℝ h x, with Mathlib's convention that this is 0 where h is not differentiable.

Statement. For n ∈ ℕ, K ≥ 0, a K-Lipschitz f : ℝⁿ → ℝ and ε ∈ (0, ∞], there is a C¹ map g : ℝⁿ → ℝ with Lⁿ({x : f(x) ≠ g(x) or Df(x) ≠ Dg(x)}) < ε.

Proof.

1. Rademacher (Simon lines 246–248). Let B := {x : f is differentiable at x}. B is Borel, being the differentiability set of a continuous map (Lean: measurableSet_of_differentiableAt). By Rademacher's theorem, Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ B) = 0 (Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.4, chapter-02.txt line 62; Lean: LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt, or Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.rademacher_ae_differentiableAt). The map Df : ℝⁿ → L(ℝⁿ, ℝ) is Borel (Lean: measurable_fderiv). Note that ε/2 ∈ (0, ∞].

2. Lusin (Simon lines 248–251). Apply the sibling theorem lusin_sigma_finite (Lean: Submission.lusin_closed_subset_continuousOn_volume) with F := L(ℝⁿ, ℝ) (finite-dimensional, with its Borel σ-algebra), u := Df, S := B and ε/2. This gives a closed C ⊆ B with Lⁿ(B ∖ C) < ε/2 such that Df|C is continuous.

3. Uniform remainder (Simon lines 251–265). C is closed, hence Borel, and for every x ∈ C ⊆ B the function f is differentiable at x with derivative Df(x) (Lean: DifferentiableAt.hasFDerivAt). Apply the sibling theorem uniform_remainder (Lean: Submission.lipschitz_uniform_remainder_on_closed_subset) to f, K, L := Df, S := C and ε/2. This gives a closed A ⊆ C with Lⁿ(C ∖ A) < ε/2 such that for every compact Q ⊆ A and ε' > 0 there is δ > 0 with |f(y) − f(x) − Df(x)(y − x)| ≤ ε'|y − x| for all x ∈ Q and y ∈ A with |x − y| < δ.

4. Whitney's hypotheses (Simon lines 264–266). On the closed set A take h := f with the gradient field Df.
- h is continuous on A, since f is Lipschitz.
- Df is continuous on A, since A ⊆ C and Df|C is continuous.
- The estimate of Step 3 is exactly 1.6(‡): R(x, y) → 0 as y → x with y ∈ A, uniformly for x in each compact subset of A.
In Lean these three facts are the fields continuous_value, continuous_derivative and remainder of Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.HasWhitneyC1Compatibility A f (fderiv ℝ f). The remainder field has literally the form of the conclusion of Step 3.

5. Whitney extension (Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.6, chapter-02.txt lines 173–184). Whitney's theorem (Lean: Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.exists_contDiff_one_extension_of_whitney, module Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.WhitneyExtension) gives g : ℝⁿ → ℝ with g ∈ C¹(ℝⁿ) (ContDiff ℝ 1 g), g = f on A, and HasFDerivAt g (Df(a)) a for every a ∈ A. Hence Dg(a) = Df(a) for all a ∈ A (Lean: HasFDerivAt.fderiv).

6. Measure estimate. By Step 5, every x with f(x) ≠ g(x) or Df(x) ≠ Dg(x) lies outside A. Since A ⊆ C ⊆ B, we have ℝⁿ ∖ A ⊆ (ℝⁿ ∖ B) ∪ (B ∖ C) ∪ (C ∖ A). Therefore Lⁿ({f ≠ g} ∪ {Df ≠ Dg}) ≤ Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ B) + Lⁿ(B ∖ C) + Lⁿ(C ∖ A) < 0 + ε/2 + ε/2 = ε. The strict inequality holds in [0, ∞] also when ε = ∞, because then Lⁿ(B ∖ C) < ε/2 and Lⁿ(C ∖ A) < ε/2 are finite (Lean: ENNReal.add_lt_add, ENNReal.add_halves). ∎

Lean remark. The module Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.WhitneyExtension is not imported by the frozen contract and has no prebuilt .olean in the pinned package tree, although its dependencies WhitneyJet and WhitneyPartition are built. Adding the import compiles it; this was checked against the pinned Mathlib and takes about 25 s.
proof_key_steps: Rademacher: the differentiability set B is Borel of full measure, and Df is Borel.
Sibling Lusin with u = Df on S = B and ε/2: closed C ⊆ B, Lⁿ(B ∖ C) < ε/2, Df|C continuous.
Sibling uniform_remainder with L = Df on S = C and ε/2: closed A ⊆ C, Lⁿ(C ∖ A) < ε/2, remainder estimate 1.6(‡) on A.
HasWhitneyC1Compatibility A f Df and SimonGMT's Whitney extension: a C¹ g with g = f and Dg = Df on A.
The exceptional set lies in (ℝⁿ ∖ B) ∪ (B ∖ C) ∪ (C ∖ A), of measure < 0 + ε/2 + ε/2 = ε.
